extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners; patent prosecutors and applicants (patent attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examiner guidance from MPEP §706.07(b) on when a final rejection may properly be made in a first Office action (including continuing/substitute applications, RCEs, and CPAs/design cases). Covers required claim relationships to earlier filings, exceptions, interview practice, form paragraphs, and shortened statutory-period handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection on first Office action for new continuing or substitute applications
rubrics_metrics.description: For a new application, claims may be finally rejected in the first Office action when (A) the new application is a continuing application of, or a substitute for, an earlier application, and (B) all claims of the new application (1) are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with, the claims in the earlier application (in other words, restriction (including lack of unity) would not have been proper if the new or amended claims had been entered in the earlier application), and (2) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criterion requires both the continuity/unity relationship to the earlier application and that, on the basis of the art and grounds already of record, the claims would have been properly finally rejected in the next action had they been entered earlier. The parenthetical explanations (e.g., 'restriction (including lack of unity) would not have been proper') clarify the unity/restriction test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final rejection on first action following Request for Continued Examination (RCE, 37 CFR 1.114)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims may be finally rejected in the first action following the filing of the RCE (with a submission and fee under 37 CFR 1.114) when all the claims in the application after entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.114 and any entered supplemental amendments (A) are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with the claims in the application prior to the entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.114 (in other words, restriction (including lack of unity of invention) would not have been proper if the new or amended claims had been entered prior to the filing of the RCE), and (B) would have been properly finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the application prior to the filing of the RCE under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both the pre- and post-RCE claim sets must be essentially the same in unity/patentable distinctness and the record must support that a final rejection would have been proper in the next action absent the RCE. The paragraph emphasizes that an RCE is not a vehicle to obtain continued examination on a different invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using RCE to switch inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot use an RCE to obtain continued examination on the basis of claims that are independent and distinct from, or lack unity of invention with, the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., applicant cannot switch inventions). See 37 CFR 1.145 and MPEP § 706.07(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an explicit limit: an RCE cannot be used to introduce a new, distinct invention as a surrogate for continued prosecution of a different invention. The MPEP cites regulatory authority and cross-references the section on restrictions/other-invention practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper to make final a first Office action when previously-denied amendments raised new issues or new matter (continuing/substitute apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action in a continuing or substitute application where that application contains material which was presented in the earlier application after final rejection or closing of prosecution but was denied entry because (A) new issues were raised that required further consideration and/or search, or (B) the issue of new matter was raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment was previously refused entry in the parent application because it raised new issues or new matter, then a first-action final rejection in the continuing/substitute application is not proper. This identifies the anti-pattern of finalizing when the record contains previously refused material that would require additional search/consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper to make final a first Office action after an RCE when pre-RCE denied entry raised new issues or new matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Similarly, it would not be proper to make final a first Office action after the filing of an RCE where material was presented after final rejection or closing of prosecution and prior to the filing of the RCE, but was denied entry because (A) new issues were raised that required further consideration and/or search, or (B) the issue of new matter was raised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors the continuing/substitute-app rule for the RCE context: previously-denied material that raised new issues or new matter prevents a first-action final rejection following the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation-in-part (CIP) rule: new subject matter prevents first-action final
rubrics_metrics.description: It would not be proper to make final a first Office action in a continuation-in-part application where any claim includes subject matter not present in the earlier application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If any claim in a CIP contains new subject matter that was not in the parent application, a first-action final rejection is improper because the claim set is not solely a continuation/substitute of the earlier disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interview practice for continuing or substitute applications prior to first action
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for an interview prior to first action on a continuing or substitute application should ordinarily be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner practice: interview requests before first action are generally allowable in these contexts; this is procedural guidance encouraging examiner engagement before finalizing a first action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.41 — Action Is Final, First Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph text: 'This is a [1] of applicant’s earlier Application No. [2]. All claims are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with the invention claimed in the earlier application (that is, restriction (including lack of unity) would not be proper) and could have been finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the earlier application. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action in this case. See MPEP § 706.07(b). Applicant is reminded of the extension of time policy as set forth in 37 CFR 1.136(a).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) Insert either '--continuation--' or '--substitute--' in bracket 1 as appropriate. (2) If an amendment was refused entry in the parent case on the grounds that it raised new issues or new matter, this form paragraph cannot be used. (3) This form paragraph should not be used in reissue litigation cases (SSP- 1 month) or in reexamination proceedings (SSP-1 or 2 months). (4) 37 CFR 1.136(a) should not be available in a reissue litigation case and is not available in reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.41.03 — Action Is Final, First Action Following Submission Under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (CPA in Design Application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph text for design CPA: 'All claims are identical to or patentably indistinct from the invention claimed in the parent application prior to the filing of this Continued Prosecution Application under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (that is, restriction would not be proper) and could have been finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action after the filing under 37 CFR 1.53(d). Applicant is reminded of the extension of time policy as set forth in 37 CFR 1.136(a).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Notes: (1) This form paragraph is for a first action final rejection in a Continued Prosecution Application filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d) (design applications only). (2) This form paragraph must be preceded by one of form paragraphs 2.30 or 2.35, as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 7.42.09 — Action Is Final, First Action Following Request for Continued Examination under 37 CFR 1.114
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph text: 'All claims are identical to, patentably indistinct from, or have unity of invention with the claims in the application prior to the entry of the submission under 37 CFR 1.114 (that is, restriction (including a lack of unity of invention) would not be proper) and all claims could have been finally rejected on the grounds and art of record in the next Office action if they had been entered in the application prior to entry under 37 CFR 1.114. Accordingly, THIS ACTION IS MADE FINAL even though it is a first action after the filing of a request for continued examination and the submission under 37 CFR 1.114. See MPEP § 706.07(b). Applicant is reminded of the extension of time policy as set forth in 37 CFR 1.136(a).'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: This form paragraph is for a first action final rejection following a Request for Continued Examination filed under 37 CFR 1.114. Use when the RCE context conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory period for reply to a first-action final
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period for reply to this final action is set to expire THREE MONTHS from the mailing date of this action. In the event a first reply is filed within TWO MONTHS of the mailing date of this final action and the advisory action is not mailed until after the end of the THREE-MONTH shortened statutory period, then the shortened statutory period will expire on the date the advisory action is mailed, and any extension fee pursuant to 37 CFR 1.136(a) will be calculated from the mailing date of the advisory action. In no event, however, will the statutory period for reply expire later than SIX MONTHS from the mailing date of this final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical effect: the normal shortened-period-for-reply (three months) applies; filing a first reply within two months can shift the expiration to the advisory action mailing date (affecting extension fee calculation), but the reply period cannot be extended beyond six months. Cross-reference 37 CFR 1.136(a) for extension fee rules; note exceptions where 1.136(a) is inapplicable (e.g., certain reissue/reexamination contexts).
